title: Longevity Channel Playbook and Deprecation Matrix for Runtime, API, SDKs, Console
creator: Maya Chen
description:
This ticket creates a single operational playbook and explicit deprecation/support matrix for Redwood's longevity channels across four product surfaces: runtime, public API, client SDKs, and Console. Goal: a predictable upgrade experience for customers and internal teams; clear SLOs for maintenance windows and backports; and automation hooks for rollout gates and upgrade tooling.

Scope:
- Define channel taxonomy (Stable, LTS, Maintenance, End-of-Life) and criteria for promotion/demotion.
- Produce a support matrix mapping versions -> supported channels -> upgrade window and guarantees.
- Specify rollout gate definitions (canary %, telemetry checks, rollback criteria) and automation points in CI/CD.
- Outline upgrade tooling: in-place compatibility checks, SDK versioning rules, migration helpers, and Console upgrade orchestration.
- Create doc templates and alerting playbooks for customers and support teams.
acceptance_criteria: Channel taxonomy documented with clear promotion/demotion rules for each surface
Support matrix published that maps specific major/minor versions to LTS and maintenance windows
Rollout gate definitions implemented in CI templates and example GitHub Actions workflow
Upgrade automation prototypes for runtime and SDKs checked in (feature branch) with integration tests
Console migration checklist and API compatibility validation included in release notes template

decisions: Adopt 3 active channels: Stable (fast cadence), LTS (24 months security + patch support), Maintenance (6 months after LTS), EOL
Runtime LTS will accept critical security patches and major performance backports only; feature backports not guaranteed
API surface will maintain semantic versioning per public endpoint; SDKs will follow independent minor-semver mapping but must declare minimum runtime API compatibility
Console releases pinned to an LTS alignment table; Console UI will feature an explicit 'Upgrade advisor' tied to the support matrix

risks: Customers with long upgrade cycles may depend on deprecated SDKs — mitigation: 'migration hints' and extended support path for paid customers
Rolling runtime patches into LTS may introduce instability — mitigation: mandatory canary and battery of regression checks before promotion
Ambiguity between API minor changes and SDK compatible versions — mitigation: stricter release checklist and automated compatibility linter
Operational overhead of multiple active channels could increase release toil — mitigation: automation for gating and clear owner matrix

migration_matrix:
Format: Version -> Surface -> Channel -> Support window (months) -> Backport policy

runtime-2.2 -> Runtime -> LTS -> 24 -> security+perf backports only
runtime-2.3 -> Runtime -> Stable -> 6 -> feature+security
api-v1.8 -> API -> LTS -> 24 -> security only; client-facing changes require deprecation notice
api-v1.9 -> API -> Stable -> 6 -> feature+security
sdk-js-3.4 -> SDK -> Maintenance -> 6 -> critical fixes only; developer migration guide required
console-2025.11 -> Console -> LTS -> 12 -> security patches + critical UX fixes

Note: This CSV will be exported to a machine-readable matrix and surfaced in the Console 'Upgrade advisor'
rollback_criteria: Primary rollback triggers (automated): error rate spike > 1.5x baseline sustained for 5m, P95 latency regression > 30%, telemetry assertion failures from canary checks. Manual rollback decision: sustained customer-impacting errors or data-loss risk. All rollbacks must create a postmortem and a remediation ticket.
automation_hooks: CI gating action 'canary-metrics' that pauses rollouts pending telemetry checks
Compatibility linter that verifies SDK/API compatibility matrix before publish
Release-note generator that injects matrix entries into customer emails and Console modal
Backport cherry-pick workflow template for LTS releases
